name: Impressed Typography
description: Words with weight. Raised fibres, quiet recesses and ink under pressure: an interactive study of material, impression and raking light.

assets.credit: Original typographic study; system fonts rendered on the device
assets.license: MIT artwork; no font binaries distributed

compatibility: WebGL with fragment high precision for normal-derived lighting and bounded ray shadows. If unavailable, real high-contrast text replaces the surface.
Mouse, trackpad, keyboard arrows and touch input. No autoplay; reduced motion starts paused. All controls and readable text remain available without the depth effect.
Uses only locally available system serif, sans-serif and monospace families. No fonts are downloaded or redistributed. Font metrics can differ between devices.
Demand-driven rendering with one full-screen draw call, two textures and twenty bounded shadow samples. Text masks rebuild only for typography changes.
PNG exports the current simulated surface. SVG is a simplified diffuse-lighting implementation with embedded raster height maps, not editable vector glyph outlines.
notes: A glyph alpha mask becomes a rounded height field. Finite differences compute its surface normals; a directional light and bounded height-field shadow tracing reveal actual positive or negative relief.
Emboss raises the same paper material. Deboss reverses the height field. Letterpress forms a shallower recess with grain-dependent ink coverage and darker edge accumulation.
Six material presets adjust paper tone, fibre character and specular response. Roughness supplies fine microrelief; the same light affects both paper and letters.
The illustrated plate descends to contact before pressure deepens the impression. The plate lifts while the impression remains. The entire sequence is a deterministic function of its scrubber.
This is a 2.5D optical simulation viewed from above, not a full deformation solver or a calibrated physical press. The section drawing exaggerates depth to explain the mechanism.
reuse: Download the source package and serve example.html over HTTP. No package install, CDN or font service is needed.
Use createImpression(canvas, settings) for an isolated surface, or mount(host, settings) for the full printing bench.
README.md documents text layout, lighting coordinates, typography controls, SVG limitations, cleanup and external integration.
Save settings locally through the Lab inspector, import/export JSON, or take PNG and SVG proofs directly from the bench.
